text: dsh-purge 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 桌面端的本机插件，通过宿主插件入口注册提示词钩子、斜杠命令和状态工具，并在设置页提供状态、补丁、配置、技能与诊断页签，同时在主区提供演练台入口。它可查看插件状态，并通过命令和桌面设置界面管理补丁、配置及本地技能；另提供会话回退入口。适合希望在 DSH 桌面端集中查看本机插件状态和管理界面的用户。需要本机安装 DeepSeek Harness 桌面端和 Node.js；本插件没有声明 API 密钥或外部服务依赖。

dsh-purge is a local DSH desktop plugin with a Settings section for status, patches, configuration, skills, and diagnostics, plus a main-area evaluation workspace. It also provides management commands. Requires the local DSH desktop app and Node.js; no API key or external service is declared.
想在 DSH 桌面端查看本机插件和补丁的状态。
I want one desktop settings page to inspect my DSH plugin status and configuration.
dsh-purge 的功能「桌面状态与管理界面」：在 DSH 桌面设置中提供状态、补丁、配置、技能和诊断页签，并提供主区演练台入口。用户可从设置界面查看本机状态并进入相应管理面板。
dsh-purge 的维护与更新元数据：已归档；距最后推送 15 天；提交数 1；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 22/100（置信度 low）。

dsh-purge README · 这是什么：装在官方 [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/harness/) 桌面端上的插件，用于网络安全红队评测。

Harness 不只是把问题交给模型：它还会在运行时改提示词、审批门、沙箱和会话格式。只看「模型答不答」，会把**宿主拦截**误当成**模型拒绝**。这个插件把两层分开——补丁把宿主那侧的拦截挪开或改写成可继续，模型那侧的回答才反映模型本身。用于受控评测，也用来看默认策略该不该收紧。

三块界面：

| 位置 | 是什么 |
| --- | --- |
| 设置页里的 `dsh-purge` 一节 | 五个页签，见下表 |
| 主区演练台 | 点侧栏图标后占满主区：授权后看资产、技能与本机环境 |
| 侧栏图标 | 入口本身；未授权时先给授权窗，不给空壳 |

设置页的五个页签：

dsh-purge README · 这是什么：| 页签 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 状态 | 结论句、补丁计数、运行环境、需要时的「重启宿主」 |
| 补丁 | 按层展开的每一条及其状态与原因 |
| 配置 | 更新、提示词注入、服务器名单、Hooks 拦截、危险操作（还原 / 卸载） |
| 技能 | 随包技能与本地技能，就地编辑 |
| 诊断 | 审计轨、安装健康、三条日志轨的落点与保留代数 |

补丁 66 条，另有 26 个永久保留的 `id` 空洞（共 92 个 `id` 守恒）。插件只动**本机已装好的**官方 `@deepseek-ai` 包与本机配置：它不是公网扫描器，也不是打别人站点的套件，仓库里没有木马、没有对外攻击载荷。

dsh-purge README · 怎么装：```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add .        # 在本仓库根目录执行
```

然后**完全退出桌面端**（含托盘），再打开。补丁在启动时自动应用。

给别的机器装，先打 tarball 再拷过去：

```sh
npm pack                                  # 产出 dsh-purge-<版本>.tgz
dsh plugin --profile desktop add ./dsh-purge-<版本>.tgz
```

环境要求：Node.js ≥22.13、dsh 0.2.1-rc.2。npm 上没有这个包，不要 `pnpm add dsh-purge`；也不要用 `dsh://` 或任何公网一键安装链接。

dsh-purge README · 装完在哪看：1. 设置左栏多出 `dsh-purge` 一节，页头「已生效」，页脚「上次应用」不是「从未」。
2. 侧栏出现演练台图标。
3. 聊天里 `/purge status` 打出的 `DSH_HOME` 是**你正在跑的那一份**。

页头显示「需重载」或「部分跳过」时，那一节里会写清是哪一条、为什么。显示「部分跳过」不影响其余补丁生效。

dsh-purge README · 常用命令：```sh
dsh-purge --status | --apply | --revert | --unseal | --uninstall | --diagnose | --edit
```

```
/purge status | apply | revert | uninstall | edit | help
/rules list | use <id> | create <id> | delete <id> | reset | help
/skills list | import <压缩包或文件夹> | create <id> [说明] | delete <id> | help
/rewind

界面里没有「应用」按钮（2.0.0 起就没有）：装完自动应用，要重来时用上面的命令。输入框旁的「回退一次 / 回退上一轮」走官方 `session.fork({ atSeq })`：撤回那一轮，新会话接上之前的上下文，旧会话归档，那句话回到输入框。
dsh-purge README · 常用命令：极简 / PTC 与标准不一致时，通常是 preset 里的拦截句没洗净：`/purge revert` → `/purge apply` → 完全退出宿主再打开 → 新开一轮对话。只换 preset 不重应用，旧进程里的补丁不会更新。

dsh-purge README · 还原、卸载、更新：- **还原**：`dsh-purge --revert`。每个目标文件在应用前备份为 `<文件>.dshpurge.bak`，还原用备份覆盖回去并删除备份；`prompt-inject.md` 是你的文件，还原时保留。
- **卸载**：设置节 → 页脚 →「卸载」，或 `/purge uninstall`。会先还原已应用的补丁，再删注入文件、规则库与插件本身，然后重启宿主。
- **更新**：换掉本机副本 → `dsh-purge --revert` → `dsh-purge --apply` → 完全退出宿主再打开。重复应用是幂等的。

**在线更新默认关闭**：设置页的「检测更新」显示「本地版：不检查更新」，不发出任何网络请求，代码里没有硬编码远端仓库。要启用得显式给 `DSH_PURGE_UPDATE_REPO=owner/name` 或 `package.json` 的 `dsh.updateSource`。

dsh-purge README · 适配范围：只支持**官方桌面端**，只支持 **dsh 0.2.1-rc.2**（`package.json` 的 `dshTarget`）。插件启动时读宿主 `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 的版本并比对：主次版本不同即**拒绝应用**，同 minor 内允许 rc 序号向上漂移；版本不对时显示原因，不会乱改文件。

`dsh web` CLI 宿主面自 1.0.0 起不再维护，那个 profile 不再更新——迁移到桌面端即可，数据留在原处。

找不到安装树时按这个顺序找：`DSH_HOME` / `DSH_BASE` → dsh 启动器旁的 `.dsh` → `npm prefix -g` / `npm root -g` → 嵌套的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai` → `~/.dsh`。都找不到就提示设置 `DSH_BASE`，不改文件。
dsh-purge README · 适配范围：运行时文件在 `$DSH_HOME`：`prompt-inject.md`、`rules/`、`skills/`、`net-scope-allow.txt`、`redteam/`、`audit/`。

dsh-purge README · 自己的服务器：中国大陆、香港、澳门的地址默认禁止，只有事先登记的那一台可以例外——在对话里说「这是我的服务器」不会放行，密钥和密码也不会。

登记在**配置**页签的服务器名单里，每行一台：`203.0.113.10`（一个 IP）、`my-vps.example.com`（主机名，保存时它的解析结果也会放行）、`alice@my-vps.example.com`（账号只用来认出这种写法，不能证明机器属于你）。保存后写入 `$DSH_HOME/net-scope-allow.txt`；密钥、密码、网段与通配符会在保存时丢掉。

dsh-purge README · 手动安装：命令行装不上、或 `dsh` 不在 PATH 时用这个。只改**正在用的那个宿主**对应的 profile。
四步，逐条照做 **1. 找到真正在用的 `$DSH_HOME`**：目录名是 `.dsh`（偶见 `dsh-home`），里面有 `profiles/`，且 `profiles/desktop/package.json` 的 `"name"` 是 `dsh-profile-desktop`。本机常有两份 `.dsh`，要认**你实际启动**的那一份。 **2. 把插件放到 `$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-purge`**（目录名与包名都必须是 `dsh-purge`，复制整个目录，不要只拷几个 `.js`）。

dsh-purge README · 手动安装：**3. 只改 `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop/package.json` 两处**（先备份）：`dependencies` 加 `"dsh-purge": "file:../../plugins/dsh-purge"`；`dsh.profile.bundles` 末尾追加 `"dsh-purge"`。原有依赖与 bundle 一个都不要删，`"dsh-purge"` 不要写两次。 **4. 在 `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop` 里 `pnpm install`**，成功标志是出现 `node_modules/dsh-purge/package.json`。然后完全退出桌面端再打开。
交给 AI 助手（只安装） 安装 DeepSeek Harness 插件 `dsh-purge`，只装到官方桌面端的 profile。不要全盘搜索，不要读或改其它文件，也不要重启应用。

dsh-purge README · 手动安装：`dsh` 不在 PATH 就告诉用户后停止。当前目录已是本仓库时用 `.`。profile 不存在就告诉用户先启动一次桌面端。npm 上没有这个包，不要 `pnpm add dsh-purge`。

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add .
```

命令结束后提醒用户：完全退出桌面端再打开，补丁会在启动时自动应用；打开宿主设置里的 `dsh-purge` 一节确认状态。然后停止。

dsh-purge README · Introduction：Install once; no button to press afterwards. Patches apply themselves when the host starts, and the UI is one new section in host Settings plus a drill page in the main area.

This page answers three things: **how to install, where to look afterwards, how to roll back**. To change this repository, read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and the [docs index](docs/文档索引.md).
dsh-purge README · What this is：A plugin for the official [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/harness/) desktop app, built for network-security red-team evaluation.

dsh-purge README · What this is：Harness does more than hand your question to a model: it rewrites prompts, approval gates, sandboxes and session formats at runtime. Judging only "did the model answer" mistakes a **host interception** for a **model refusal**. This plugin separates the two layers — patches move or rewrite the host-side interception, so the model-side answer reflects the model. It is for controlled evaluation, and for judging whether default policy should be tightened.

Three pieces of UI:

dsh-purge README · What this is：| Where | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| The `dsh-purge` section in Settings | Five tabs, listed below |
| Drill page in the main area | Opening the sidebar icon fills the main area: assets, skills and local environment after authorization |
| Sidebar icon | The entry point itself; it shows an authorization dialog instead of an empty shell |

The five tabs:

dsh-purge README · What this is：| Tab | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| Status | Verdict line, patch counts, runtime environment, "restart host" when needed |
| Patches | Every patch by layer, with its state and reason |
| Configuration | Updates, prompt injection, server allowlist, Hooks interception, dangerous actions (revert / uninstall) |
| Skills | Bundled and local skills, edited in place |
| Diagnostics | Audit track, install health, the three log tracks with their locations and retained generations |

dsh-purge README · What this is：66 patches plus 26 permanently retired `id` holes (92 `id`s conserved). The plugin only touches the official `@deepseek-ai` packages **already installed on this machine**, and local configuration: it is not an internet scanner and not a kit for attacking other people's sites. The repository ships no trojan and no outbound attack payload.

dsh-purge README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add .        # run in this repository's root
```

Then **quit the desktop app completely** (including the tray) and open it again. Patches apply at startup.

For another machine, pack a tarball and copy it over:

```sh
npm pack                                  # produces dsh-purge-<version>.tgz
dsh plugin --profile desktop add ./dsh-purge-<version>.tgz
```
dsh-purge README · Install：Requirements: Node.js ≥22.13, dsh 0.2.1-rc.2. The package is not on npm — do not `pnpm add dsh-purge`, and do not use `dsh://` or any public one-click install link.

dsh-purge README · Where to look afterwards：1. Settings gains a `dsh-purge` section, header state is "Applied", footer "last applied" is not "never".
2. A drill icon appears in the sidebar.
3. `/purge status` in chat prints the `DSH_HOME` of the host **you are actually running**.

If the header says "reload needed" or "partially skipped", that section names the patch and the reason. "Partially skipped" does not stop the other patches from applying.

dsh-purge README · Commands：```sh
dsh-purge --status | --apply | --revert | --unseal | --uninstall | --diagnose | --edit
```

```
/purge status | apply | revert | uninstall | edit | help
/rules list | use <id> | create <id> | delete <id> | reset | help
/skills list | import <zip or folder> | create <id> [note] | delete <id> | help
/rewind

dsh-purge README · Commands：There is no "Apply" button in the UI (none since 2.0.0): installation applies automatically, and the commands above are for re-running it. "Rewind one turn / previous turn" next to the input box uses the official `session.fork({ atSeq })`: the turn is withdrawn, a new session continues with the earlier context, the old one is archived, and that prompt returns to the input box.

dsh-purge README · Commands：When minimal / PTC disagrees with standard, it is usually an interceptor line left in the preset: `/purge revert` → `/purge apply` → quit the host fully and reopen → start a new conversation. Swapping the preset without re-applying leaves the old process patched.

dsh-purge README · Revert, uninstall, update：- **Revert**: `dsh-purge --revert`. Every target file is backed up as `<file>.dshpurge.bak` before patching; revert restores from the backup and deletes it. `prompt-inject.md` is your file and survives a revert.
- **Uninstall**: Settings section → footer → "Uninstall", or `/purge uninstall`. It reverts applied patches, deletes the injection file, rule library and the plugin, then restarts the host.
- **Update**: replace the local copy → `dsh-purge --revert` → `dsh-purge --apply` → quit the host fully and reopen. Applying twice is idempotent.

dsh-purge README · Revert, uninstall, update：**Online updates are off by default**: "Check for updates" reports "local build: no update check" and sends no network request; no remote repository is hard-coded. Enable it only by setting `DSH_PURGE_UPDATE_REPO=owner/name` or `dsh.updateSource` in `package.json`.

dsh-purge README · Compatibility：Official desktop app only, and only **dsh 0.2.1-rc.2** (`dshTarget` in `package.json`). At startup the plugin reads the host's `@deepseek-ai/dsh` version and compares: a different major.minor means it **refuses to apply**; within the same minor, rc numbers may drift upward. On mismatch it shows the reason and touches no files.

The `dsh web` CLI surface has not been maintained since 1.0.0; that profile is no longer updated — move to the desktop app, your data stays where it is.

dsh-purge README · Compatibility：When the install tree is not found it probes in this order: `DSH_HOME` / `DSH_BASE` → the `.dsh` next to the dsh launcher → `npm prefix -g` / `npm root -g` → nested `@deepseek-ai/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai` → `~/.dsh`. If none exists it asks you to set `DSH_BASE` and changes nothing.

Runtime files live in `$DSH_HOME`: `prompt-inject.md`, `rules/`, `skills/`, `net-scope-allow.txt`, `redteam/`, `audit/`.

dsh-purge README · Your own servers：Addresses in mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau are blocked by default; only the machine you registered beforehand is exempt. Saying "this is my server" in a conversation does not unblock anything, and neither do keys or passwords.

dsh-purge README · Your own servers：Register it in the server allowlist on the **Configuration** tab, one per line: `203.0.113.10` (a single IP), `my-vps.example.com` (a hostname; whatever it resolves to at save time is allowed too), `alice@my-vps.example.com` (the account part only identifies the notation, it does not prove ownership). Saving writes `$DSH_HOME/net-scope-allow.txt`; keys, passwords, CIDR ranges and wildcards are dropped on save.

dsh-purge README · Manual install：Use this when the command line is unavailable or `dsh` is not on PATH. It only touches the profile of the host **you are actually running**.
Four steps, in order **1. Find the real `$DSH_HOME`**: a `.dsh` directory (occasionally `dsh-home`) containing `profiles/`, where `profiles/desktop/package.json` has `"name": "dsh-profile-desktop"`. Machines often have two `.dsh` copies; pick the one **you actually launch**.

dsh-purge README · Manual install：**2. Put the plugin at `$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-purge`** (directory name and package name must both be `dsh-purge`; copy the whole directory, not a few `.js` files).

**3. Edit only two places in `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop/package.json`** (back it up first): add `"dsh-purge": "file:../../plugins/dsh-purge"` under `dependencies`, and append `"dsh-purge"` to the end of `dsh.profile.bundles`. Delete nothing that was already there and do not list `"dsh-purge"` twice.

dsh-purge README · Manual install：**4. Run `pnpm install` inside `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop`** — success means `node_modules/dsh-purge/package.json` exists. Then quit the desktop app fully and reopen it.
Hand it to an AI assistant (install only) Install the DeepSeek Harness plugin `dsh-purge` into the official desktop profile only. Do not search the disk, do not read or modify other files, and do not restart the application.

dsh-purge README · Manual install：If `dsh` is not on PATH, tell the user and stop. If the current directory is this repository, use `.`. If the profile does not exist, tell the user to launch the desktop app once. The package is not on npm; do not run `pnpm add dsh-purge`.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add .
```

After the command, remind the user to quit and reopen the desktop app (patches apply at startup) and to confirm the state in the host Settings `dsh-purge` section. Then stop.

"Rewind one turn / previous turn" next to the input box uses the official `session.fork({ atSeq })`: the turn is withdrawn, a new session continues with the earlier context, the old one is archived, and that prompt returns to the input box.

dsh-purge README · Revert, uninstall, update：- **Revert**: `dsh-purge --revert`. Every target file is backed up as `<file>.dshpurge.bak` before patching; revert restores from the backup and deletes it. `prompt-inject.md` is your file and survives a revert.
- **Uninstall**: Settings section → footer → "Uninstall", or `/purge uninstall`. It reverts applied patches, deletes the injection file, rule library and the plugin, then restarts the host.
- **Update**: replace the local copy → `dsh-purge --revert` → `dsh-purge --apply` → quit the host fully and reopen. Applying twice is idempotent.

dsh-purge README · Revert, uninstall, update：**Online updates are off by default**: "Check for updates" reports "local build: no update check" and sends no network request; no remote repository is hard-coded. Enable it only by setting `DSH_PURGE_UPDATE_REPO=owner/name` or `dsh.updateSource` in `package.json`.

At startup the plugin reads the host's `@deepseek-ai/dsh` version and compares: a different major.minor means it **refuses to apply**; within the same minor, rc numbers may drift upward. On mismatch it shows the reason and touches no files.

The `dsh web` CLI surface has not been maintained since 1.0.0; that profile is no longer updated — move to the desktop app, your data stays where it is.

dsh-purge README · Your own servers：Register it in the server allowlist on the **Configuration** tab, one per line: `203.0.113.10` (a single IP), `my-vps.example.com` (a hostname; whatever it resolves to at save time is allowed too), `alice@my-vps.example.com` (the account part only identifies the notation, it does not prove ownership). Saving writes `$DSH_HOME/net-scope-allow.txt`; keys, passwords, CIDR ranges and wildcards are dropped on save.

dsh-purge README · Introduction：Install once; no button to press afterwards. Patches apply themselves when the host starts, and the UI is one new section in host Settings plus a drill page in the main area.

This page answers three things: **how to install, where to look afterwards, how to roll back**. To change this repository, read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and the [docs index](docs/文档索引.md).
dsh-purge README · What this is：A plugin for the official [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/harness/) desktop app, built for network-security red-team evaluation.

dsh-purge README · What this is：Harness does more than hand your question to a model: it rewrites prompts, approval gates, sandboxes and session formats at runtime. Judging only "did the model answer" mistakes a **host interception** for a **model refusal**. This plugin separates the two layers — patches move or rewrite the host-side interception, so the model-side answer reflects the model. It is for controlled evaluation, and for judging whether default policy should be tightened.

Three pieces of UI:

dsh-purge README · What this is：| Where | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| The `dsh-purge` section in Settings | Five tabs, listed below |
| Drill page in the main area | Opening the sidebar icon fills the main area: assets, skills and local environment after authorization |
| Sidebar icon | The entry point itself; it shows an authorization dialog instead of an empty shell |

The five tabs:

dsh-purge README · What this is：| Tab | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| Status | Verdict line, patch counts, runtime environment, "restart host" when needed |
| Patches | Every patch by layer, with its state and reason |
| Configuration | Updates, prompt injection, server allowlist, Hooks interception, dangerous actions (revert / uninstall) |
| Skills | Bundled and local skills, edited in place |
| Diagnostics | Audit track, install health, the three log tracks with their locations and retained generations |

dsh-purge README · What this is：66 patches plus 26 permanently retired `id` holes (92 `id`s conserved). The plugin only touches the official `@deepseek-ai` packages **already installed on this machine**, and local configuration: it is not an internet scanner and not a kit for attacking other people's sites. The repository ships no trojan and no outbound attack payload.

dsh-purge README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add .        # run in this repository's root
```

Then **quit the desktop app completely** (including the tray) and open it again. Patches apply at startup.

For another machine, pack a tarball and copy it over:

```sh
npm pack                                  # produces dsh-purge-<version>.tgz
dsh plugin --profile desktop add ./dsh-purge-<version>.tgz
```
dsh-purge README · Install：Requirements: Node.js ≥22.13, dsh 0.2.1-rc.2. The package is not on npm — do not `pnpm add dsh-purge`, and do not use `dsh://` or any public one-click install link.

dsh-purge README · Where to look afterwards：1. Settings gains a `dsh-purge` section, header state is "Applied", footer "last applied" is not "never".
2. A drill icon appears in the sidebar.
3. `/purge status` in chat prints the `DSH_HOME` of the host **you are actually running**.

If the header says "reload needed" or "partially skipped", that section names the patch and the reason. "Partially skipped" does not stop the other patches from applying.

dsh-purge README · Commands：```sh
dsh-purge --status | --apply | --revert | --unseal | --uninstall | --diagnose | --edit
```

```
/purge status | apply | revert | uninstall | edit | help
/rules list | use <id> | create <id> | delete <id> | reset | help
/skills list | import <zip or folder> | create <id> [note] | delete <id> | help
/rewind

dsh-purge README · Commands：There is no "Apply" button in the UI (none since 2.0.0): installation applies automatically, and the commands above are for re-running it. "Rewind one turn / previous turn" next to the input box uses the official `session.fork({ atSeq })`: the turn is withdrawn, a new session continues with the earlier context, the old one is archived, and that prompt returns to the input box.

dsh-purge README · Commands：When minimal / PTC disagrees with standard, it is usually an interceptor line left in the preset: `/purge revert` → `/purge apply` → quit the host fully and reopen → start a new conversation. Swapping the preset without re-applying leaves the old process patched.

dsh-purge README · Revert, uninstall, update：- **Revert**: `dsh-purge --revert`. Every target file is backed up as `<file>.dshpurge.bak` before patching; revert restores from the backup and deletes it. `prompt-inject.md` is your file and survives a revert.
- **Uninstall**: Settings section → footer → "Uninstall", or `/purge uninstall`. It reverts applied patches, deletes the injection file, rule library and the plugin, then restarts the host.
- **Update**: replace the local copy → `dsh-purge --revert` → `dsh-purge --apply` → quit the host fully and reopen. Applying twice is idempotent.

dsh-purge README · Revert, uninstall, update：**Online updates are off by default**: "Check for updates" reports "local build: no update check" and sends no network request; no remote repository is hard-coded. Enable it only by setting `DSH_PURGE_UPDATE_REPO=owner/name` or `dsh.updateSource` in `package.json`.

dsh-purge README · Compatibility：Official desktop app only, and only **dsh 0.2.1-rc.2** (`dshTarget` in `package.json`). At startup the plugin reads the host's `@deepseek-ai/dsh` version and compares: a different major.minor means it **refuses to apply**; within the same minor, rc numbers may drift upward. On mismatch it shows the reason and touches no files.

The `dsh web` CLI surface has not been maintained since 1.0.0; that profile is no longer updated — move to the desktop app, your data stays where it is.

dsh-purge README · Compatibility：When the install tree is not found it probes in this order: `DSH_HOME` / `DSH_BASE` → the `.dsh` next to the dsh launcher → `npm prefix -g` / `npm root -g` → nested `@deepseek-ai/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai` → `~/.dsh`. If none exists it asks you to set `DSH_BASE` and changes nothing.

Runtime files live in `$DSH_HOME`: `prompt-inject.md`, `rules/`, `skills/`, `net-scope-allow.txt`, `redteam/`, `audit/`.

dsh-purge README · Your own servers：Addresses in mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau are blocked by default; only the machine you registered beforehand is exempt. Saying "this is my server" in a conversation does not unblock anything, and neither do keys or passwords.

dsh-purge README · Your own servers：Register it in the server allowlist on the **Configuration** tab, one per line: `203.0.113.10` (a single IP), `my-vps.example.com` (a hostname; whatever it resolves to at save time is allowed too), `alice@my-vps.example.com` (the account part only identifies the notation, it does not prove ownership). Saving writes `$DSH_HOME/net-scope-allow.txt`; keys, passwords, CIDR ranges and wildcards are dropped on save.

dsh-purge README · Manual install：Use this when the command line is unavailable or `dsh` is not on PATH. It only touches the profile of the host **you are actually running**.
Four steps, in order **1. Find the real `$DSH_HOME`**: a `.dsh` directory (occasionally `dsh-home`) containing `profiles/`, where `profiles/desktop/package.json` has `"name": "dsh-profile-desktop"`. Machines often have two `.dsh` copies; pick the one **you actually launch**.

dsh-purge README · Manual install：**2. Put the plugin at `$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-purge`** (directory name and package name must both be `dsh-purge`; copy the whole directory, not a few `.js` files).

**3. Edit only two places in `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop/package.json`** (back it up first): add `"dsh-purge": "file:../../plugins/dsh-purge"` under `dependencies`, and append `"dsh-purge"` to the end of `dsh.profile.bundles`. Delete nothing that was already there and do not list `"dsh-purge"` twice.

dsh-purge README · Manual install：**4. Run `pnpm install` inside `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop`** — success means `node_modules/dsh-purge/package.json` exists. Then quit the desktop app fully and reopen it.
